en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammānulomapaccanīya (3), Tikapaṭṭhānapāḷi (1) 13.6.
Vitakkattika (The Triplet on Applied Thought)

Dependent on a state with applied thought and sustained thought (savitakka-savicāra), a state without applied thought and sustained thought (na-savitakka-na-savicāra) arises by way of root condition (hetu-paccaya).
Dependent on a state with applied thought and sustained thought, a state without applied thought but with sustained thought only (na-avitakka-vicāramatta) arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state with applied thought and sustained thought, a state without applied thought and sustained thought arises by way of root condition.

Dependent on a state with applied thought and sustained thought, states that are neither with applied thought and sustained thought nor without applied thought and sustained thought arise by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state with applied thought and sustained thought, a state without applied thought but with sustained thought [arises]...
And states that are neither with initial application nor sustained application arise conditioned by root-cause.

Dependent on a state with initial application and sustained application, states that are neither with initial application and sustained application nor without initial application but with sustained application arise conditioned by root-cause.

Dependent on a state with initial application and sustained application, states that are neither with initial application and sustained application nor without initial application but with sustained application... [arise].
States that are neither with applied thought nor sustained thought arise by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state with applied thought and sustained thought only, a state that is neither with applied thought nor sustained thought arises by way of root condition.

Dependent on a state with applied thought and sustained thought only, a state that is neither with applied thought nor sustained thought arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a state with applied thought and sustained thought only, a state that is with applied thought and sustained thought arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state that is without applied thought but with sustained thought, there arises a state that is without applied thought and without sustained thought by way of root condition.

Dependent on a state that is without applied thought but with sustained thought, there arise states that are both with applied thought and with sustained thought and neither with applied thought nor with sustained thought by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state that is without applied thought but with sustained thought, [there arises] a state that is without applied thought but with sustained thought...
And states that are neither with applied thought nor sustained thought arise by way of root-cause condition.

Dependent on a state that has no applied thought but has sustained thought, states that are neither with applied thought and sustained thought nor without applied thought and sustained thought arise by way of root-cause condition.

Dependent on a state that has no applied thought but has sustained thought, states that are neither with applied thought and sustained thought nor without applied thought and sustained thought... [arise].
And states that are neither with initial application nor sustained application arise by way of root condition.

Dependent on a state without initial application and without sustained application, a state that is neither with initial application nor sustained application arises by way of root condition … (seven).

Dependent on a state both with initial application and sustained application and a state without initial application and without sustained application, a state that is neither with initial application nor sustained application arises by way of root condition … (seven).

Dependent on states that are without applied thought but with sustained thought (*avitakkavicāramatta*) and without both applied and sustained thought (*avitakka-avicāra*), a state that is neither with applied nor sustained thought (*nasavitakkasavicāra*) arises by way of root condition (*hetupaccaya*) … [etc. … seven.

Dependent on states that are both with applied and sustained thought (*savitakkasavicāra*) and without applied thought but with sustained thought, a state that is neither with applied nor sustained thought arises by way of root condition … [etc. … seven.

Dependent on states that are both with applied and sustained thought, without applied thought but with sustained thought, and without both applied and sustained thought, a state that is neither with applied nor sustained thought arises by way of root condition … [etc. … seven. (Abbreviated.)

In the case of the root condition, there are forty-nine; in the object condition, forty-nine; in the predominance condition, thirty-two …pe… in the prenascence and repetition conditions, twenty-five …pe… in the non-disappearance condition, forty-nine.
(The "Conascent Chapter" and the "Investigation Chapter" should also be expanded in detail.)
